   City Council Regular Meeting Agenda
  Tuesday, August 16, 2022

 •  CALL TO ORDER
 •  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE LED BY: Mayor Ding
 •  ROLL CALL: Mayor Ding, Vice Mayor Harrington, Council Members Menchaca,
  Rivera, Wu

 1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

 2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. UPPER SAN GABRIEL VALLEY MUNICIPAL WATER DISTRICT
  PRESENTATION ABOUT EMERGENCY CONSERVATION INITIATIVES AND
  DROUGHT CONDITIONS

 3. PUBLIC COMMENT

 4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  All items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and
  recommendations will be approved in one motion unless a member of the
  City Council or audience requests separate discussion.

  A. RESOLUTION NO. 22-52 REAUTHORIZING THE CITY COUNCIL AND THE
  CITY’S COMMISSIONS TO IMPLEMENT TELECONFERENCE ACCESSIBILITY
  FOR CONDUCTING PUBLIC MEETINGS PURSUANT TO ASSEMBLY BILL 361

  Resolution No. 22-52 makes findings that allow the City to continue
  implementation of teleconference/internet-based accessibility for public
  meetings under state-of-emergency provisions.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 22-52 regarding
  the use of teleconferencing for public meetings.

  B. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council
  meeting.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – August 16, 2022  2
   1. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of July 19, 2022.
  2. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of July 19, 2022.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

  C. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The most recent Material Demands from the Finance Department are presented
  to the City Council for review and approval.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Material Demands as
  presented.

  D. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT – JULY 2022

  In accordance with the City of San Gabriel’s 2022-23 Adopted Investment Policy
  (Resolution No. 22-30) and California Government Code Section 53646, the
  Finance Director is to render an investment report to the City Council, City
  Treasurer, City Manager, and the City Attorney. The July 2022 Cash and
  Investment Report is presented to receive and file in accordance with the City’s
  adopted 2022-23 Investment Policy.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the Cash and
  Investment Report for July 2022.

  E. LEAGUE OF CALIFORNIA CITIES ANNUAL CONFERENCE RESOLUTIONS
  PACKET

  On April 5, 2022, the City Council appointed Mayor Tony Ding as the Delegate
  and Council Member John Wu as the Alternate to serve as the City’s voting
  delegate for the League of California Cities. Each year, the League of California
  Cities accepts resolutions from member cities and elected officials to be voted
  on at its annual conference. This year, the League of California Cities (Cal Cities)
  Board of Directors voted to present proposed bylaws amendments to the
  General Assembly during the 2022 Cal Cities Annual Conference and Expo. At
  least two-thirds of the General Assembly must vote in favor of the proposed
  bylaws amendments for them to take effect. There is no fiscal impact for this
  item.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – August 16, 2022  3
   Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the voting delegate and voting
  alternate to use their discretion to vote on potential petitioned resolutions and
  the League’s proposed bylaws amendments.

  F. ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NOS. 22-47 AND 22-48 SETTING THE RATE
  AND AMOUNT NECESSARY FOR THE 2022-23 FISCAL YEAR RETIREMENT
  LEVY

  The City’s retirement costs are funded by a special property tax levy authorized
  by the voters in 1948. The special property tax levy approved by the voters
  requires the City Council to annually establish a tax rate sufficient to meet the
  City’s obligations to the state employees’ retirement system. No Change in the
  tax rate is recommended for the 2022-23 Fiscal Year and the City Council is
  asked to confirm the current rate and fix the amount of property taxes to be
  generated by adopting two resolutions. Based on the assessed valuation
  ($6,489,280,378) – an increase of 6.1% over (Fiscal Year 2021-22 value) prepared
  by the Auditor Controller and the recommended continued levy of 14 cents per
  $100 of assess property value, the amount to be generated is estimated at
  $9,084,993 for Fiscal Year 2022-23. This levy, along with the current fund
  balance in the Retirement Fund, will be sufficient to cover the retirement costs,
  budgeted at $9,366,652 for Fiscal Year 2022-23.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 22-47, setting the
  tax rate at 14 cents per $100 assessed valuation, and Resolution No. 22-48,
  fixing the amount of property taxes to be generated for the City’s employees’
  retirement cost for Fiscal Year 2022-23.

  G. PURCHASE AND INSTALLATION OF UPDATED PARKING PERMIT PAY
  STATIONS IN THE AMOUNT OF $46,502.62 FROM PACIFIC PARKING
  SYSTEMS

  The City is currently utilizing two parking permit pay stations purchased from
  Pacific Parking Systems, Incorporated (formerly Pacific Parking Installations) in
  2004. The outdated pay stations are not capable of accepting credit card
  payments or giving adequate change, creating a significant inconvenience to
  residents and visitors seeking to purchase parking permits. Pacific Parking
  Systems is a well-established vendor and offers the lowest price compared to
  VenTek International and Northwest Parking Equipment Company. The

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – August 16, 2022  4
   purchase of new overnight parking permit pay stations is currently budgeted in
  Police Department’s Special Project Fund #124-751-15-261 and the fiscal
  impact for Fiscal Year 22-23 is $46,502.62.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends the City of San Gabriel purchase three venSTATION C2-GC
  pay stations from Pacific Parking Systems, Incorporated with installation and
  associated annual fees.

  H. PURCHASE OF TWO ELECTRIC JOHN DEERE GATOR TE UTILITY VEHICLES
  IN THE AMOUNT OF $29,341.67 FOR THE PARKS DIVISION

  The Parks Division within the Public Works Department is responsible for the
  operation and maintenance of the City’s parks and park facilities. The City has
  six park locations with open areas for residential recreation. These park areas
  have designated picnic shelters with restroom facilities as well as designated
  sports courts and fields. The Parks Division, with the help of Facilities staff,
  maintains the daily operations of our parks, including restroom maintenance,
  trash pickup and on-going landscape maintenance. Currently, the Parks
  Division has three Gator utility vehicles, but two will be sent to auction due to
  their age, condition, and on-going upkeep costs. Staff is seeking approval to
  purchase two new John Deere Gator TE 4x2 electric utility vehicles from Deere
  & Company through a Sourcewell Awarded Contract. The total cost for both
  utility vehicles is $29,341.67.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council waive formal bidding and authorize the
  Cooperative Purchase Agreement for two John Deere Gator TE 4x2 electric
  utility vehicles, consistent with the piggyback bidding requirements pursuant
  to Municipal Code Section 34.35, and authorize the City Manager to approve a
  Purchase Order with Deere and Company in an amount not to exceed
  $29,341.67 from the Air Quality Management District budget account #124-
  800-51-99-922.

  I. A MEMORANDUM OF AGREEMENT WITH THE SAN GABRIEL VALLEY
  COUNCIL OF GOVERNMENTS FOR PARTICIPATION IN THE SAN GABRIEL
  VALLEY REGIONAL FOOD RECOVERY PROGRAM

  The passage of Senate Bill 1383 (Lara, 2016) (SB 1383) implemented statewide
  targets to reduce statewide disposal of organic waste and increase recovery of

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – August 16, 2022  5
   currently disposed edible food for human consumption. Specifically, SB 1383
  aims to recover at least 20% of currently disposed edible food for human
  consumption by 2025. To recover 20% of edible food that would otherwise be
  sent to landfills by 2025, SB 1383 requires local jurisdictions to establish food
  recovery programs and strengthen their existing food recovery networks.
  Approval of a Memorandum of Agreement with the San Gabriel Valley Council
  of Governments to Participate in a Regional Food Recovery Program will allow
  a regional approach toward compliance with SB 1383’s food recovery
  components by enhancing the capacity of local food recovery organizations to
  recover edible food waste and provide outreach and education activities. There
  will be no fiscal impact on the General Fund.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to execute
  a Memorandum of Agreement between the City of San Gabriel and the San
  Gabriel Valley Council of Governments.

  J. VALLEY BOULEVARD AND  DEL  MAR  AVENUE  INTERSECTION
  IMPROVEMENTS PROJECT

  The City of San Gabriel is proposing improvements to the intersection of Valley
  Boulevard and Del Mar Avenue as part of the State Route 710 (SR-710) North
  Mobility Improvement Projects (MIP). Improvements to the intersection would
  include lane reconfiguration, intersection corner improvements, lengthening of
  turn lanes on Valley Boulevard, vegetation and on-street parking removal, the
  addition of continental crosswalks, and the synchronization of traffic signals
  along Valley Boulevard. Environmental impacts have been evaluated and a draft
  Mitigated Negative Declaration has been prepared for this project for Council’s
  consideration. There are no fiscal impacts to the general fund associated with
  the recommended action.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt a Mitigated Negative Declaration
  and Mitigation Monitoring and Reporting Program.

  K. RESOLUTION NO. 22-53 APPROVING A REQUEST FOR TEMPORARY
  STREET CLOSURE ON THE 300 BLOCK OF BRIDGE STREET

  The Public Works Department received a request from Raymond Lieu, resident
  at 329 Bridge Street, for a temporary street closure. The purpose of this request

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – August 16, 2022  6
   is to hold a Labor Day Celebration block party which will be held on Sunday,
  September 4, 2022, on the 300 block of Bridge Street from 3:00 p.m. to 8:00
  p.m. There is no fiscal impact to the budget for this event.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 22-53 authorizing
  closure on Bridge Street between Sycamore Drive to the end of the cul-de-sac
  from 3:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. on Sunday, September 4, 2022.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING – None.

 6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

 7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. RESOLUTION NO. 22-50 APPROVING TEMPORARY CLOSURE OF
  COMMERCIAL AVENUE ON SEPTEMBER 11, 2022, A TEMPORARY USE
  PERMIT (TUP) FOR THE STUNTS AND FUN EVENT, AND AUTHORIZING
  CITY SUPPORT FOR THE EVENT

  The City received a request from Sammy Maloof of Maloof Racing, on behalf of
  the Stuntman’s Association (Applicant), for a Temporary Use Permit (TUP) and
  street closure for a private event called Stunts and Fun, to be held on Sunday,
  September 11, 2022 from 10:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. on Commercial Avenue. This
  event will take place on Commercial Avenue from San Gabriel Boulevard to the
  east end of the street. The goal of the event is to raise funds to help those in
  need due to COVID-19. This is a free, no-cost event that is open to the public.
  In addition to the TUP and street closure, the Applicant is also requesting the
  City support the event in the form of the City providing staff support.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 22-50 approving
  temporary closure of Commercial Avenue between Gladys Avenue and the
  Rubio Wash from 10:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. on Sunday, September 11, 2022; a
  Temporary Use permit (TUP) for the Stunts and Fun event; and authorizing City
  support for the event.

  CITY COUNCIL OPTIONS

  As an alternative to the staff recommendation, the City Council has two options:

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – August 16, 2022  7
   1. Decide that the event is a private event instead of a City-sponsored event,
  and require the Applicant to pay for staff time and expenses.
  2. Decide that the street closure event is not in the best interests of the City
  and deny the Applicant’s request to hold the event.

  B. FUND BALANCE RESERVE POLICY AMENDMENT

  A key component of a well-managed organization is a written policy that
  stipulates prudent fund balance reserve levels. The fund balance reserve policy
  supports proactive financial management and is a strategic tool to fund certain
  and uncertain future expenditures. A vigilant attempt has been made to identify
  future expenditures and to develop strategies to address each identified need
  within the policy. The fund balance reserve policy has been amended to address
  those identified certain and uncertain future expenditures. There is no fiscal
  impact for this item.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 22-54 amending
  the fund balance reserve policy.

  C. FISCAL YEAR END PRELIMINARY FINANCIAL RESULTS UPDATE – JUNE 30,
  2022

  This report provides the preliminary financial results for the City’s General Fund
  for fiscal year ending June 30, 2022. The presented General Fund financial
  results present the projected revenues, expenditures and ending fund balance
  for the General Fund. The numbers are currently being audited and additional
  adjustment may be made to the financial results. Audited financial statements
  will be completed by December 31, 2022 and presented to the City Council in
  January 2023. There is no fiscal impact related to this item.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council review and file the report.

  D. POLICE ANNUAL UPDATE

  The Police Department will be presenting an update to the City Council on
  August 16, 2022. This is a presentation item only and there is no staff report for
  this item.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – August 16, 2022  8
   E. ORDINANCE NO. 684 ADOPTING POLICE DEPARTMENT LEXIPOL POLICY,
  SECTION 707, MILITARY EQUIPMENT, PURSUANT TO ASSEMBLY BILL (AB)
  481 MILITARY EQUIPMENT ACQUISITION, USE, AND REPORTING -
  INTRODUCTION

  In the wake of several high-profile incidents, recent policing reform efforts have
  resulted in changes in legislation that directly impact policing in the City of San
  Gabriel. As a result of emerging concerns related to the use of military-style
  equipment by local law enforcement, and the requisite oversight and
  accountability, Assembly Bill 481 was passed. It mandates certain requirements
  for the acquisition, use, and funding of military-style equipment. On July 19,
  2022 Council provided temporary approval governing the continued use of
  equipment already in possession and use by the Police Department until the
  matter could be brought back to be adopted or ordinance. Such Ordinance is
  now before the Council for consideration.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council read by title only, waive further reading,
  and introduce Ordinance No. 684 entitled, “An Ordinance of the City Council of
  San Gabriel, California, adopting Police Department Lexipol Policy, Section 707,
  Military Equipment, pursuant to Assembly Bill (AB) 481 Military Equipment
  Acquisition, Use, and Reporting” and schedule the second reading and
  adoption for the next City Council meeting.

 8. PUBLIC COMMENT

 9. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

 10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of

  report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

 11. CLOSED SESSION – None.

 12. ADJOURNMENT

  The next regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, September 6, 2022

  Economic Development Manager Caroline Velarde made the presentation .

  Applicant Stanley Maloof on behalf of the Stuntmen's Association, presented
  information about the fund-raising event.

I  Clarifying discussion included how donations would be collected; no admission fee
  would be charged; City exposure to liability; how many City employees are being
  requested to work at the event; financial impact on the City should the City sponsor
  the event; safety provisions; and fees charged for private events, with a deposit
  required for staff cost.

  Chasity Jennings-Nunez, resident, provided comments  in  opposition to City
  support of the private event.

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 4 of 7  August 16, 2022
   Discussion included that the fees required do not include staff time; the applicant
  has 501 c6 status; verification that donations have been made after the event;
  applicant's plan to split proceeds 50% with the City; and adding a condition of
  approval that states that 50% of the net revenue will go to the City and non-profits.

  A motion was made by Council Member Menchaca, seconded by Vice Mayor
  Harrington, to adopt Resolution No. 22-50 approving temporary closure of
  Commercial Avenue between Gladys Avenue and the Rubio Wash from 10:00 a.m.
  to 5:00 p.m. on Sunday, September 11 , 2022; approving a Temporary Use Permit

I  (TUP) for the Stunts and Fun event; and authorizing City support for the event; with
  the addition of a Condition of Approval that the applicant shall provide accurate
  accounting for the event and shall donate 50% of net revenue to the City and local
  non-profits; and amendment of Section 3 of the Resolution to state the event will
  be supported by the City in the form of the City providing staff support and waiver
  of the event fees.

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  B. FUND BALANCE RESERVE POLICY AMENDMENT

  Finance Director Kaholokula made the presentation.

  Clarifying discussion included a state policy which requires vehicle replacement

I  with clean vehicles; the City's fleet services fund includes funds for vehicle
  replacement, and restricted use for Air Quality Management District (AQMD) funds.

  There was no public comment.

  Discussion included details of why the City has higher general-fund reserves than
  expected by Fiscal Year 2021-2022 and associated impact on the state audit; the
  City Council making a decision on a new reserves amount after figures are audited;
  maximum points are received on the state audit at 50% reserves; the fleet-services
  fund has some reserves for vehicle replacement; and that a capital-replacement
  fund would be a new fund.
